findings.statement: Direct PR-288 build, check, and engines modes do not bind the imported htt.infer.bayesian_semantics module to the candidate root or registered source bytes; a preloaded replacement in sys.modules is executed despite _activate_sources(), so receipt recomputation can use code other than the source later hashed into the receipt.
assumptions_used: Runner containment requires the computation implementation and validator to originate from the candidate being attested.
A cached Python module remains authoritative to import even after candidate source directories are prepended to sys.path.
counterevidence_refs: The focused pytest subprocess replaces PYTHONPATH and portable mode scrubs it, but direct build/check/engines modes execute in the current interpreter and remain vulnerable to preloaded modules.
reproduction: Preload package-shaped htt, htt.infer, and htt.infer.bayesian_semantics objects in sys.modules; give the replacement builder a RuntimeError marker; set sys.argv to runner plus engines; execute the runner with runpy.run_path(..., run_name='__main__').
unresolved: Repair by importing only after rejecting cached modules or by validating module __file__, regular-file status, root containment, and SHA-256 against the registered candidate source before any builder or validator call; add a hostile preloaded-module regression.

findings.statement: The claim-bearing receipt metadata cannot record an exact candidate identity or exact generating command: the runner hard-codes generation_identity=EXTERNAL_CANDIDATE_SEAL_OR_SOURCE_HASHES, the validator whitelists only three placeholder literals, and generating_procedure says engines even though build writes the receipt.
assumptions_used: The governing minimum metadata requires git commit or worktree state and the generating procedure for a claim-bearing frozen numerical artifact.
A label promising an external seal or source hashes is not itself the identity of either.
counterevidence_refs: The receipt separately binds four source-file hashes, but git_commit_or_worktree_state still contains only the placeholder and generating_procedure remains factually wrong.
reproduction: Inspect runner _build(): every build passes EXTERNAL_CANDIDATE_SEAL_OR_SOURCE_HASHES.
Inspect _expected_claim_metadata(): any exact candidate SHA is rejected as an unregistered generation identity, while the stored generating procedure is the non-writing engines mode.
unresolved: Accept an exact sealed candidate/tree/source-binding identity, validate its syntax and relationship to the source bindings, record the exact build argv, and regenerate the receipt only after the final candidate and real mandatory Dynesty execution are fixed.

findings.statement: Portable replay uses tarfile.extractall(..., filter='data') even though the package advertises Python >=3.10; this interface is available in the audited Python 3.12 runtime, but the runner has no compatibility path or minimum-version guard for supported 3.10/3.11 environments.
assumptions_used: Portable semantics must cover every supported Python minor or explicitly narrow the supported floor.
Safe extraction cannot be restored by blindly dropping the filter argument.
evidence_refs: runtime-probe:Python 3.12.3 TarFile.extractall signature includes keyword-only filter
counterevidence_refs: The current Python 3.12.3 environment accepts the call; no Python 3.10 or 3.11 execution evidence was available in this assignment.
reproduction: Compare htt/pyproject.toml requires-python >=3.10 with the unconditional filter='data' call in portable mode.
Run the portable extraction path under the declared minimum Python versions after implementing a version-compatible safe extractor or raising the supported floor.
unresolved: Add a safe 3.10/3.11 extraction implementation and minimum-version CI, or explicitly raise requires-python and all installation metadata consistently.
